title: Lightwell v0: decisions and first non-destructive JPEG editor
objective: Resolve remaining M0 details, then deliver an M1 native macOS arm64 editor on the owner's M4 MacBook Pro: reference one JPEG, apply reversible geometry edits, reopen its catalog, export a new JPEG, recover a moved original with manual Locate, and support live GUI/agent editing through shared JSON commands, local IPC and MCP. Retain early Windows/Linux build coverage and the separate native portability gate.
context_summary: Planning-only handoff, updated 2026-09-19. No application code, VM installation or benchmarks exist. Owner decisions: M4 MacBook Pro first; Nikon Z6/Fujifilm X100VI RAW targets; open-source-only direction; reference existing files; first demo includes geometry edits, undo, reopen, export, live agent control and manual Locate. Crop has free handles and proportional Option scaling about its fixed center; straightening preserves composition with minimum necessary trimming. Zoom/pan, percentages and Fit are required. Export strips optional metadata by default with a Keep metadata setting. Owner edits locally then syncs to an external drive; broader storage workflows require later research. GPL-3.0-or-later is recommended but not formally applied. Workspace layout, flip/quarter-turn crop behavior, remaining UI details, framework selection, recording-mode samples and hardware configuration remain open. This plan covers M0, Mac-first M1 and a separate Windows/Linux portability gate (TASK-019). Later feature work remains in Markdown. Existing task IDs and history are preserved.

tasks.description: Resolve the owner decisions required for the feasibility trials and first editor.
extra_context: Owner decisions received 2026-09-19 are recorded in docs/decisions.md. Do not re-ask agreed hardware/cameras, open-source intent, import/demo/live-agent/Locate scope, crop resizing and straightening, export metadata defaults, or zoom/pan/percentage/Fit scope.

Remaining product choices include workspace layout, visible flip/quarter-turn crop behavior, essential aspect-ratio presets and daily workflow priorities. Formal license selection follows dependency review. Record RAM and recording modes when available without blocking unrelated work.

Expose discoverable schemas for M1 catalog/asset/session queries, geometry/history, bounded previews, export/jobs and source recovery from the shared operation registry.
Preserve expected revisions, request/retry semantics, structured failures and explicit job cancellation; keep diagnostics off protocol stdout.
Verify protocol interoperability and service parity with a real MCP client or conformance harness, including a live-GUI edit/preview/undo journey in final integration checks.

steps: Test tool discovery, invalid input, structured results, image-preview bounds and protocol lifecycle against the selected SDK/client.
Run the same recipe changes through MCP and direct service calls and compare state and rendered results.
Exercise disconnects, retries and revision conflicts without independent catalog writes.
expected_results: Verify protocol interoperability and service parity with a real MCP client or conformance harness, including a live-GUI edit/preview/undo journey in final integration checks.

tasks.description: Implement verified manual Locate through the desktop and shared command API.
extra_context: Manual Locate was explicitly selected for M1 on 2026-09-19. Folder relinking and automatic detection remain later work.
Owner edits locally then syncs back to an external drive. Do not implement file sync, automatic archive switching or library-wide scans in this task.

context_links.label: Source recovery contract
context_links.relevance: Defines identity, verification, duplicates and failure behavior.

context_links.label: First-demo recovery
context_links.relevance: Makes moved-source recovery part of the acceptance journey.

acceptance_criteria: Show missing-source state and manual Locate without removing the existing asset, recipe or history; preserve labelled cached previews when available.
Verify the selected source against the stored full fingerprint with bounded cancellable I/O, rejecting mismatches and files changed during verification.
Atomically relink matching moved/renamed files or explicit byte-identical copies, handle an already-cataloged candidate without silent merging, and retain geometry undo history.
Expose the same source recovery through the shared schema/command registry and update all live clients after a successful locator change.
UI and programmatic tests recover the same asset/edits across moves and an external-volume copy while preserving state on mismatch, cancellation, conflicts or failed commit.

steps: Import/edit a fixture, rename or move it and relink it; compare asset ID, recipe, history and export.
Test a byte-identical copy, a same-name different image, duplicate asset identity and concurrent source modification.
Exercise cancellation, unavailable volume and failed locator persistence; verify GUI/MCP parity in final integration.
expected_results: UI and programmatic tests recover the same asset/edits across moves and an external-volume copy while preserving state on mismatch, cancellation, conflicts or failed commit.
